results.title: The Dragon in the West
creator: Daniel Ogden
results.description: The book describes the evolution of the modern dragon from its ancient forebears, in terms both of its form and of its narrative contexts. In physical form dragons are broadly serpentine, but have animalian heads, thick central bodies, wings, and clawed legs. In their stories they live in caves, lie on treasure, maraud, and burn; they are extraordinarily powerful, but even so ultimately worsted in their battles with humans. Despite the inestimable success of this physical form and this broad story-type, there is nothing obvious, inevitable, or natural about them. Rather, both are mature, complex, and artificial constructs. The book traces the evolution of the dragon’s form from the purely serpentine drakon of classical antiquity, through its merging with the forms of the ancient sea monster and the winged, humanoid demon, into that of the first recognizably modern dragon, the two-legged wyvern that emerged in the illustrated manuscripts of the ninth century AD, which has previously been described as the ‘Romanesque’ or ‘Gothic’ dragon. It traces the evolution of the dragon’s typical story-type again from classical antiquity, across the vast tradition of medieval hagiography (saints’ lives), and into the Germanic world, where particular attention is given to the wealth of dragons featured in the Norse sagas.

results.title: Epilogue
creator: Avalyn Hunter
results.description: The epilogue begins with the life of Rosa Hoots following Black Gold's death and continuing through increasing adversity and misfortune, including the loss of Black Gold's Kentucky Derby trophy to theft several years before her death in 1938. It then turns to Hanley Webb and his death in obscurity in 1940 before discussing J. D. Mooney's subsequent career in racing and the successes of his family after his death in 1966. It concludes with some of the traditions associated with Black Gold, ending with a description of the Fair Grounds' Black Gold Stakes and its wreath laying ceremony in honor of the Derby winner.

results.title: Baby Steps
creator: Avalyn Hunter
results.description: This chapter covers the beginning of Black Gold's racing career at the Fair Grounds in New Orleans. After discussing his impact on the early season juvenile racing at the track, it describes his maiden victory and the odd events surrounding his second race, and introduces one of his major rivals during his two-year-old season, Worthmore. It concludes by introducing the theme of Black Gold's persistent bad luck and the question of its equally persistent appearance in races in which Worthmore was involved.

results.title: Waiting Game
creator: Avalyn Hunter
results.description: The chapter begins by looking at Black Gold's continued slow training and the reasons behind it before presenting the views of various sportswriters regarding the colt's preparation. It then turns to J. D. Mooney and his acceptance of an engagement to ride Cherry Tree at the Agua Caliente track on Tijuana while waiting for the Kentucky racing season to open. A description of Agua Caliente and Tijuana in that time period follows, and then coverage of Mooney's race riding in the Coffroth Handicap and afterward, concluding with an assessment as to how the stint in Mexico impacted the skills Mooney would need to ride in the Kentucky Derby.

results.title: Ruled Off
creator: Avalyn Hunter
results.description: The chapter follows Useeit through racing in Kentucky after her winter in New Orleans and discusses Al Hoots's actions after she was claimed from him by J. W. "Bub" May at Lexington. Following Hoots's repurchase of the mare six races later, the chapter then follows the mare's misfortunes during the 1915-1916 season at Terrazas Park, which ended in her being claimed from a selling race by Tobe Ramsey. Hoots refused to honor the claim, and the chapter explores his actions and the possible reasons behind them. It ends with Hoots's decision to begin Useeit's breeding career, his final illness and death in 1917, and Rosa Hoot's promise to keep the mare and try to fulfill her husband's last wishes.

results.title: Converging Paths
creator: Avalyn Hunter
results.description: The chapter opens with the recovering Black Gold going to Lexington to prepare for the Breeders' Futurity, in which he was expected to meet Worthmore again along with a new rival in Chilhowee. The theme of Black Gold's continuing "bad luck" when facing Worthmore is examined, leading to its culmination in Worthmore's owner and jockey being suspended after their colt made a sharp turnaround in the Breeders' Futurity from losing badly to Black Gold five days earlier. The final part deals with Black Gold's increasing behavior problems and Hanley Webb's need for a jockey who could fix them, a role J. D. Mooney hoped to fill but still saw no way to obtain.
